analysis:
Compared supplied BASE/HEAD integration tests and examined the added policy-test metadata and bounded patch. CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift head:456-489 adds real-socket tests for accelerated reconnect after code 1012 and backoff reset after a stable session; head:649-726 injects policy and measures re-registration. Existing encryption, cancellation/reservation release, enrollment signatures, telemetry suppression and outbound-after-reconnect assertions remain unchanged. No production control is weakened by these test changes. Mock signatures and relaxed test privacy capabilities are pre-existing fixtures, not serving authorization. The test's 'consumer' ephemeral key represents the trusted coordinator's hop key, not consumer-to-provider end-to-end secrecy.
CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift visible patch lines 1-42 asserts stable-session reset and ordinary exponential ranges; the remainder of this added 95-line file is not supplied. CI inclusion is documented at integration-test head:10-12 but the runner/workflow is outside this batch.
Integration should examine the changed CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorClient runLoop/socket-close handling together: ensure accelerated 1012 reconnect retains jitter/bounded retry behavior (A-018, TB-002), and connection teardown still invalidates authorization and prevents stale outbound work crossing sessions (A-016, T-053). These tests prove re-registration timing, not renewed permission or proof binding. The implementation is outside supplied evidence, so its security implications remain unresolved rather than findings. No observed change affects cache scoping/encryption (T-041), model integrity, privileged fan/add-on boundaries, payment controls or plaintext exposure mitigations.
